title: Director, Quality Systems & Digital Quality
text:
Cambridge, MA

Development – Quality Assurance /

Full-Time /

Hybrid

 

*Scholar Rock is delivering muscle-targeted breakthroughs to transform the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and other rare neuromuscular diseases where muscle atrophy remains a critical unmet need.*

*As a global leader in myostatin biology, a field focused on proteins that regulate muscle mass, the biopharmaceutical company is named for the visual resemblance of a scholar rock to protein structures. Our commitment to unlock fundamentally different treatment approaches is powered by broad application of a proprietary platform, which has developed novel monoclonal antibodies to modulate protein growth factors with extraordinary selectivity. Scholar Rock works every day to create new possibilities for patients through its highly innovative anti-myostatin program, including opportunities in additional rare neuromuscular diseases. Learn more about our neuromuscular franchise at* ***ScholarRock.com*** *and follow @ScholarRock on X and on LinkedIn.*

 

**Summary of Position:**

Scholar Rock is seeking an experienced, hands-on Director, Quality Systems & Digital Quality. Reporting to the Sr Director, Global Quality Systems & Compliance, this leader is an integral part of Scholar Rock’s Quality Management System (QMS) and the GxP computerized systems and data that support it, across our commercial and early-phase pipeline. Because Scholar Rock outsources all GMP manufacturing, testing, and distribution to qualified contract organizations, this role will build and sustain a lean, risk-based, phase-appropriate QMS that meets US (FDA), EU (EMA/EU GMP), and Japan (MHLW/PMDA) requirements, ensuring that Scholar Rock’s own systems are inspection-ready and that the GxP data generated on our behalf by contract partners is reliable, complete, and traceable.

### **Position Responsibilities**

***Quality Management System***

* Partner with Quality process owners to ensure GxP digital systems effectively support QMS processes, enabling efficient, compliant, and scalable operations aligned with Scholar Rock’s evolving business needs.
* Track a focused set of key QMS performance indicators and present them in periodic quality management reviews.

 

***Digital Systems & Computer Software Assurance***

* Provide Quality oversight of Scholar Rock’s GxP computerized systems (largely cloud/SaaS, e.g., eQMS, document and training management, ERP and other GxP-relevant platforms), ensuring compliance with 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, and Japan’s ER/ES guideline.
* Lead and execute GxP system enhancements and continuous improvement initiatives, partnering with business process owners to define requirements, evaluate solutions, manage implementation, and ensure effective adoption of new functionality.
* Establish and apply a risk-based computerized system validation and assurance approach consistent with applicable GxP regulatory requirements, leveraging GAMP 5 principles, relevant FDA guidance, and vendor documentation to ensure appropriate assurance while minimizing redundant testing.
* Oversee the GxP computerized system lifecycle, including risk-based validation and assurance, change control, periodic reviews, access management, audit trail controls, data retention, and system retirement. Ensure appropriate validation deliverables, testing, and documented evidence are established and maintained throughout the system lifecycle.
* Partner with IT and business owners on system selection, implementation, upgrades, and vendor releases so that new digital capabilities are adopted with right-sized assurance.
* Support qualification of computerized system suppliers (e.g., SaaS, software, and IT service providers), including risk-based vendor assessments and audits, and the Part 11/Annex 11 and data integrity provisions of their quality agreements; qualification of GMP manufacturing and testing suppliers remains with other Quality functions.
* Monitor evolving expectations, including the revision of EU GMP Annex 11 and emerging guidance on AI in GxP settings, and advise on practical, compliant adoption of digital and AI-enabled tools.
* Support the implementation of AI-enabled tools in GxP processes (e.g., document drafting and review, deviation and complaint trending, AI features within eQMS and other platforms), defining risk-based assurance, human oversight, and data integrity controls proportionate to each tool’s intended use and impact on product quality and patient safety.
* Partner with IT, Legal, and business owners to establish lightweight governance for AI use in GxP activities, including an inventory of AI applications, acceptable-use expectations, training, and ongoing performance monitoring.
* Lead the development and execution of a risk-based digital Quality roadmap, prioritizing system enhancements and improvements based on business needs, compliance requirements, and operational efficiencies.
* Partner with Quality process owners and cross-functional stakeholders to identify improvement opportunities, translate business needs into functional requirements, and implement scalable digital solutions.
* Drive the end-to-end implementation of GxP system enhancements, including requirements definition, risk assessments, configuration, testing, validation documentation, deployment, and post-implementation support.
* Establish efficient processes for managing system changes, including vendor releases, impact assessments, regression testing, and maintaining systems in a validated state.
* Provide hands-on leadership and technical guidance for Veeva eQMS, eDMS, and other GxP platforms, ensuring effective system functionality, integration, and continuous improvement.
* Establish clear system ownership, governance, and accountability across Quality, IT, and business functions, including responsibilities for system administration, validation, user access, and ongoing lifecycle management.
* Support regulatory inspections and audits involving computerized systems, electronic records, electronic signatures, and data integrity, including preparation of supporting documentation and remediation of identified gaps.
* Drive effective adoption of new digital capabilities through stakeholder engagement, training, change management, and ongoing evaluation of system effectiveness.
* Establish and maintain effective governance for GxP system enhancements and vendor releases, including change prioritization, impact assessments, testing strategies, implementation planning, and post-deployment monitoring.

 

***Data Integrity & Data Governance***

* Lead the development and ongoing governance of Scholar Rock’s GxP data integrity program, establishing risk-based expectations, controls, and oversight mechanisms in partnership with business process owners and applicable Quality functions.
* Define a lightweight data governance model with clear data ownership and stewardship for GxP data across Quality, Regulatory, Technical Operations, and Clinical.
* Extend data integrity oversight to contract organizations through quality agreement requirements, data integrity–focused audit criteria, and review of partner-generated data (e.g., batch records, CoAs, stability, deviations).
* Establish governance and controls for GxP-relevant master data, partnering with designated data owners to ensure data accuracy, consistency, integrity, and appropriate alignment across internal systems, contract partners, and regulatory information.
* Lead data integrity risk assessments and drive timely, proportionate remediation of gaps.

 

***Inspection Readiness & Regulatory Support***

* Lead inspection readiness for the QMS, computerized systems, and data integrity controls, and support health authority inspections of Scholar Rock and its contract partners.
* Contribute to regulatory submissions and responses, such as annual reports, IND/CTA updates, and marketing applications in the US, EU, and Japan.
* Maintain awareness of regulatory changes in the US, EU, and Japan and translate them into practical, minimal-necessary updates to the QMS.

 

***Leadership & Partnership***

* Act as the subject matter expert and coach for colleagues across Quality and partner functions on QMS, computerized system, and data integrity topics.
* Collaborate with the Head of Global Quality and Quality leadership, IT, Regulatory, Technical Operations, and Clinical to align quality systems with corporate goals and regulatory obligations.
* Champion a culture of quality, accountability, and data integrity, and serve as a change agent for simplification and digitization of the QMS.

### **Candidate Requirements**

* BS/MS degree in a scientific, engineering, or information systems discipline.
* 12+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical/biotech industry, with 5+ years leading Quality systems, computerized system compliance, or related programs; biologics experience preferred.
* Deep understanding of GxP and Quality System requirements (US, EU, and Japan) for biologics development and commercial products, including ICH Q9(R1) and Q10.
* Demonstrated expertise in 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, risk-based CSA/GAMP 5, and global data integrity expectations, including qualification of computerized system and SaaS suppliers.
* Familiarity with AI/ML-enabled tools in regulated environments and with emerging health authority expectations for AI use in GxP activities.
* Experience in a virtual or outsourced model, including oversight of quality systems and data integrity at CDMOs and contract testing laboratories.
* Experience leading or supporting regulatory inspections and interfacing with global health authorities.
* Proven ability to design lean, simple processes and to make pragmatic, risk-based decisions on what is required versus nice to have.
* Highly proactive, decisive, and capable of independently managing key initiatives as a hands-on individual contributor.
* Collaborative leader who builds quality culture and capability across teams through influence, coaching, and knowledge sharing.
* Excellent communication skills and ability to influence across functions and with external partners.

$200,000 - $260,000 a year

*Scholar Rock is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees*.
